Paper: Wallace, Murphy, Hernandez-Colmenares & Fujita (2026) JPSP 130(2) 291-307, doi:10.1037/pspi0000498.
note: Level 1, both label levels read in the three .sav files that feed this table (files taken from the batch_647 cache; sha256 match the batch_647 record / OSF listing). Code derivation (data/wallace_2026_mindsets.py, fit.csv spec: fit{i} -> fit{i} for s1c, s2, s2c, no flip): item IS the source column name in all three studies, so exempt from Step 5b and no verification files. PER-STUDY VARIANTS: live cov_study 1 = Study 2 (838 ids), 4 = S1c (796), 7 = S2c (793). All three items are worded differently in every study (Study 2 about taking a course from / being in this professor's class; S1c Working at MCM Consulting; S2c Volunteering at XYZ Organization), so following the batch_644-649 convention item_text carries all three verbatim variable labels prefixed 'Study 2 (cov_study = 1): ' / 'Study S1c (cov_study = 4): ' / 'Study S2c (cov_study = 7): ' joined by ' | ' (prefixes and separator are IRW's; wording after each prefix is the label verbatim). Organization name: S1c labels say MCM Consulting (the processing script docstring says XYZ for S1c; the .sav label governs, as batch_648 also found). OPTIONS: every item in every study has value labels 1='1 - Strongly agree', 7='7 - Strongly disagree', 2-6 carry only their own digit; digit prefixes stripped and 2-6 left blank. NO RECODE for this scale (no itemcov_recoded column in the live table; all three studies print the same 1 = Strongly agree order). Route 9: all 9 study x item count vectors match source = live exactly, e.g. Study 2 fit1 76/122/121/162/149/99/109, S1c fit2 102/94/82/127/155/158/78, S2c fit3 107/153/132/161/90/69/81. Direction cross-check: the growth-mindset condition (treat=1) has LOWER means than fixed (treat=0) in every study (Study 2 3.2 vs 5.0, S1c 4.0 vs 4.3, S2c 3.2 vs 4.1), i.e. more agreement that the growth target is a good fit, consistent with 1 = Strongly agree; so a higher resp means LESS perceived fit, as labelled. No instructions text in any .sav or .sps; left blank. Rights: study-authored items, no stated restriction located (silence = permission).
public_note: Items were worded for a different target in each pooled study (a professor in Study 2, cov_study = 1; MCM Consulting in Study S1c, cov_study = 4; XYZ Organization in Study S2c, cov_study = 7), so item_text gives all three wordings labelled by study; responses run 1 = Strongly agree to 7 = Strongly disagree, so a higher value means less perceived fit.
